title: A fixed-capacity stack on raw memory
description:
Write `struct RawStack` that stores up to `capacity` `i32` values in memory it allocates itself, with a completely safe public API:

- `RawStack::new(capacity: usize) -> RawStack` allocates with `std::alloc::alloc` (using `Layout::array::<i32>(capacity)`); a capacity of 0 must not allocate (use a dangling pointer, `NonNull::dangling()`), and a failed allocation calls `std::alloc::handle_alloc_error`.
- `push(&mut self, value: i32) -> Result<(), i32>`: `Err(value)` when full.
- `pop(&mut self) -> Option<i32>` and `peek(&self) -> Option<i32>`.
- `len(&self)`, `is_empty(&self)` and `as_slice(&self) -> &[i32]` (bottom first).
- `impl Drop` frees the memory with `std::alloc::dealloc` (not for capacity 0).

Every `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment.
hints: `Layout::array::<i32>(capacity)` describes the memory for `capacity` integers; `alloc(layout)` returns a `*mut u8` that you cast to `*mut i32`. Keep it in a `NonNull<i32>` so the "never null" fact is in the type.
`ptr.add(i).write(v)` stores without reading the old (uninitialised) value; `ptr.add(i).read()` copies the value out. The first `len` slots are the only ones that are ever read.
rules: Free the memory in impl Drop for RawStack.
